subject: Seabound — multi-jurisdiction tax handling & invoice reissue
messages:

Cc: Karl Hansen <karl.hansen@seabound.io>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tax treatment for Redwood invoices (AU GST + EU VAT)

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough. Finance here — a couple of items we need to clear before we process the first invoice:

1) In Australia: we expect the supplier to issue net invoices when reverse‑charge applies. Seabound will self‑account for GST where eligible; we need Redwood to mark the invoice clearly as reverse‑charge (ABN: 66 123 456 789 attached).

2) In the EU: we have two entities — Seabound EU (NL) and Seabound UK (GB). For NL invoices we can provide a valid VAT number (attached) and require zero‑rating where applicable. For UK, please treat as B2B standard VAT handling.

3) Can Redwood reissue the July invoice split by Seabound entity so VAT lines are explicit per entity?

4) We also need confirmation on whether you validate VAT IDs in real time (VIES) and what evidence you attach to invoices for audit.

Attaching: AU GST registration, EU VAT cert.

Can you confirm steps and timeline? We are aiming to get payment out next week but can hold if documentation is pending.

Thanks,
Anna Jensen
Finance Manager
Seabound Software
attachments: Seabound_GST_registration_AU.pdf, Seabound_EU_vat_certificate.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Hi Anna —

Appreciate the clear notes and the attachments — very helpful. Short answer: yes, we can handle reverse‑charge display and we perform VAT ID checks against VIES for EU numbers; for AU we rely on ABN confirmation plus customer attestation.

Looping in Neha (tax) and Kimberly (finance ops) to confirm the exact reissue flow and timing.

Proposed next steps from our side:
- Neha to confirm whether Seabound's EU VAT number validates in VIES (and capture a validation snapshot for the invoice).
- Kimberly to propose invoice split (entity mapping + new invoice numbers) and whether we need a credit note for the original invoice.
- I'll attach the Redwood vendor form if your procurement wants it signed.

I'll follow up with a single action list and ETA by EOD Monday.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Tax treatment for Redwood invoices (AU GST + EU VAT)

Ben/Kim —

I validated the EU VAT number provided by Seabound (NL) against VIES this morning. Result: valid (validation id: VIES-20260713-0912). I captured a screenshot and will include the validation id on the reissued invoice as audit evidence.

AU ABN: we accept the scanned GST registration + customer self‑attestation. For the AU reverse‑charge we need a line on the invoice: "Reverse charge — recipient to account for GST under section X" (we have standard wording used for prior customers).

Couple of policy notes:
- If Seabound wants zero‑rated EU supply, they must confirm intra‑EU B2B movement and provide an accepted VAT registration. We have a checklist; I can share it.
- For accounting, we recommend VS invoice split: bill Seabound NL from our EMEA billing entity; bill Seabound AU from Redwood APAC entity. That allows local tax treatment and easier payment routing.

I will prepare the reissue template and the VIES snapshot. Let me know if finance wants a temporary credit hold while we reissue.

Neha Kapoor
Tax & Compliance
Redwood Inference
attachments: (VIES-20260713-0912-snapshot.png)

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:02:00 +0200
Subject: RE: Tax treatment for Redwood invoices (AU GST + EU VAT)

Ben / Neha —

Thanks, quick clarifications from our side:
- Seabound NL will accept a reissued zero‑rated invoice if the VAT number and VIES snapshot are included.
- For Australia: we confirm Seabound is not registered as an Australian entity — we are an offshore customer purchasing services. We will self‑account for GST under reverse charge; please include the standard reverse‑charge wording.
- We prefer the invoice split (NL vs APAC) so treasury can route payments to the appropriate bank accounts.

Also: can Redwood mark the original invoice as "void — to be reissued" and issue new invoice numbers? That avoids double‑payment in our AP system.

Karl
VP Finance
Seabound Software

Anna/Karl —

We can do the void + reissue approach. Proposed finance actions and ETA: 

1) Void original invoice INV-20260701-998 (will be marked "Void — Reissued").
2) Create two new invoices:
   - INV-20260713-1001 (billed to Seabound NL, zero‑rated VAT line + VIES reference)
   - INV-20260713-1002 (billed to Seabound APAC, reverse‑charge wording for GST)
3) Attachments included on both invoices: VIES validation snapshot and the customer ABN / attestation as provided.
4) If you need a credit hold while payment reallocation happens, Marissa can set a 7‑day hold on collection.

Marissa — please confirm account hold option and whether we require a signed vendor form before we accept bank routing changes. Ben — I'm attaching Redwood_vendor_form.xlsx for your procurement.

Kimberly Park
